sheets.subject: Uruk, Southern Mesopotamia, about 3000 BCE (Late Uruk period): the town of Uruk seen from across a canal: a dense spread of flat-roofed mud-brick houses and courtyards among date palms, and above them the White Temple: a white-plastered temple standing on a very high mud-brick platform with sloping plain sides (not a stepped ziggurat). No city wall. Low and wide.

Uruk, Southern Mesopotamia, about 3000 BCE (Late Uruk period): (1) an irrigation canal seen across from the side: calm water between raised earth banks, 1.2 m high; (2) the edge of a field of ripe barley with a few date palms behind it, 2 m high; (3) a muddy canal bank with a broken gap where water leaks out, 1 m high.

Uruk, Southern Mesopotamia, about 3000 BCE (Late Uruk period): the temple precinct (Eanna): (1) a thick temple courtyard wall of mud brick whose lower half is covered with a mosaic of clay cones pressed into the plaster in zigzag and diamond patterns (red, black and cream cone heads), with a plain doorway, 4 m high; (2) a row of round columns completely covered in the same clay-cone mosaic, 4 m high.

Uruk, Southern Mesopotamia, about 3000 BCE (Late Uruk period): inside a temple storeroom office: (1) a plain mud-brick inner wall with a low bench along it, reed baskets full of small clay tablets on the bench, a small doorway with daylight, 3 m high; (2) a beaten-earth floor strip with a reed mat, 0.4 m high.

Uruk, Southern Mesopotamia, about 3000 BCE (Late Uruk period): a temple grain store, each a separate object: (1) a tall stack of plain, thick, rough clay bowls with sloping sides and a bevelled rim (bevelled-rim bowls), nested upside down, 0.8 m high; (2) a large heap of barley grain, 1 m high; (3) a row of three tied grain sacks, 0.9 m high; (4) a tall plain storage jar, 1.1 m high.

Uruk, Southern Mesopotamia, about 3000 BCE (Late Uruk period): each a separate object: (1) two oxen side by side under a wooden yoke pulling a simple wooden plough (an ard: a plain wooden plough with one handle, no seed funnel), 1.5 m high, 3.5 m long; (2) a reed boat with a high curved prow loaded with grain sacks, empty of people, 1.4 m high, 6 m long.

Uruk, Southern Mesopotamia, about 3000 BCE (Late Uruk period): small objects as a tidy specimen sheet, each separate: (1) a small flat clay tablet with rounded corners, with a few pressed picture signs on it (an ear of barley, a sheep's head, round number marks), 0.08 m; (2) a single plain rough clay bowl with sloping sides and a bevelled rim, 0.1 m high; (3) a stone cylinder seal beside a strip of clay with its rolled pattern of animals, 0.06 m; (4) a reed stylus, 0.2 m; (5) a curved sickle made of fired clay, 0.3 m; (6) a tall alabaster vase carved in bands: water at the bottom, barley and palms, sheep, people carrying baskets, 1 m high.
